extra_powers: Can cause one verifier of the message endpoint to attest arbitrary messages; this system represents that capability as control of one verifier key.
limits: Cannot change governance decisions, contract configuration or deployed code.

trusted: Governance sets the collateral price correctly for a fully backed token.
Contracts are deployed exactly as written, with the configuration in the source.
honest_parties: Every other verifier is operated independently of the attacker's verifier, by a different entity on separate infrastructure, and attests only messages that match an actual event on the source chain.
environment: The collateral price is set by governance; there is no oracle to manipulate.
excluded: Bugs on the source chain or in its contracts.
More than one verifier compromised at once.
How the attacker obtains that verifier capability; only its effect, one verifier attesting arbitrary messages, is modelled.
Economic effects such as bank runs, and gas or denial-of-service griefing against these contracts.
threat_model.property: Given independently operated verifiers, no sequence of transactions by this attacker mints unbacked collateral or makes the protocol under review lose lender funds.

root_cause.detail: the endpoint is deployed with one verifier and one required confirmation, so one compromised verifier can approve a forged message

0-target.assumes: the collateral token is backed by ETH locked elsewhere

1-upstream.guarantees: supply grows only through delivered messages

2-upstream.guarantees: a message is delivered after 1 of 1 verifier confirmations

propagation_path: 2-upstream: MessageEndpoint.deliver accepts a forged message with one confirmation
1-upstream: BridgedRestakeToken.receiveMessage mints tokens with nothing locked behind them
0-target: LendingPool.borrow lends real ETH against the unbacked tokens
0-target: LendingPool.withdrawEth reverts for honest lenders once liquidity is gone
expected_reviewer_finding: The pool accepts a bridged token as collateral whose minting depends on a single-verifier message check two dependencies upstream; forged mints let an attacker borrow all lender liquidity.
simplifications: One endpoint with a confirmation threshold instead of real cross-chain messaging and token-bridge code
Collateral price set by governance instead of an exchange-rate oracle
No interest, liquidation or multi-asset pools; stablecoin-pool withdrawals are not modelled
Amounts are illustrative, not the incident's

The attacker's capability is modelled as a controlled verifier key. LayerZero's incident report describes tampered RPC responses and a denial of service on an external RPC provider that led the single verifier to attest a forged message; that upstream compromise is abstracted away (https://layerzero.network/blog/layerzero-labs-kelpdao-incident-report).

The mock token mints new tokens when a message is delivered. In the incident the Ethereum-side adapter released existing rsETH without a matching burn on the source chain, leaving remote-chain claims under-backed, so the backing deficit arose in the adapter's locked balance rather than through new supply (https://governance.aave.com/t/rseth-incident-report-april-20-2026/24580).
